title: Specification Primitive
description: A design specification produced by brainstorm mode or grill sessions. Defines what to build, not how. Stored in docs/specs/<name>.md.

purpose.description: What changes for the user? What does success look like?

constraints.description: Performance, security, deadlines, budgets, compatibility requirements.
constraints.shape: array of { category: string, requirement: string }

architecture.description: Components, boundaries, data flow, and the domain model. The domain model has two halves. The semantic half is what exists: object types, their properties, and the link types between them. The kinetic half is what may change: action types, the only way an object is modified. A spec that models only the semantic half produces read-only schemas that every component then mutates at will, which is where domain invariants die.

shape.components: array of { name: string, responsibility: string, boundaries: string[] }
shape.dataFlow: description of how data moves between components
shape.objectTypes: array of { name: string, definition: string, identity: string, properties: array of { name: string, type: string, units?: string } }
shape.linkTypes: array of { name: string, from: string, to: string, cardinality: 'one-to-one' | 'one-to-many' | 'many-to-many', inverse: string }
shape.actionTypes: array of { name: string, objectType: string, changes: string[], validates: string[], sideEffects: string[], repeatBehavior: 'idempotent' | 'rejects-duplicate' }
shape.interfaces: array of { name: string, shape: string, implementedBy: string[] }

failureModes.shape: array of { scenario: string, impact: string, mitigation: string }

testing.description: What proves correctness. The command or surface that shows it, not a required test.
testing.shape: array of { test: string, proves: string }

migration.description: How this ships without breaking prod.
migration.shape: array of { step: string, rollback: string }

reversibility.description: What does 'back out' look like if it goes wrong?

validationRules.allRequiredSectionsPresent: purpose, scope, architecture, and failureModes must all be non-empty
validationRules.scopeIsExhaustive: in + out + deferred must cover the full problem space — nothing unaddressed
validationRules.failureModesNonTrivial: at least one failure mode beyond 'the whole thing crashes'
validationRules.alternativesAcknowledged: if alternatives were discussed, the rejected ones must appear in an alternatives section
validationRules.everyMutationIsAnAction: every state change in dataFlow names an actionType; a component with no actionType does not write
validationRules.everyLinkHasAnInverse: each linkType names its inverse, so traversal works in both directions
validationRules.everyActionValidates: each actionType lists at least one validation and states whether repeating it is idempotent
validationRules.interfaceHasTwoImplementations: an interface is declared only when at least two object types share the shape; one implementation is a rename
